text.p: German drugmaker Schering AG said Tuesday its provisional group net profits jumped 46 percent last year to a record-breaking 362 million marks ($217.7 million), significantly ahead of its own forecasts for the year.

The world's largest manufacturer of oral contraceptives said sales increased 13 percent to 5.27 billion marks ($3.2 billion) , of which 791 million marks ($476 million) came from its domestic market and 4.48 billion ($2.7 billion) came from abroad.
The company said its operating profits were hurt by restructuring costs of 60 million marks ($36 million).
"The main engine for growth was higher sales at our U.S. and European units. In Latin America we profited from better economic conditions in key markets," it said.
In January, Schering's chief financial officer said he expected net profit of about 330 million to 340 million marks ($199 million to $205 million) for 1996, a rise of more than 35 percent.
